subject: NordicBank RFP: Deployment footprint & data residency clarifications

Subject: NordicBank RFP: Deployment footprint & data residency clarifications

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking the team's initial RFP. We're pulling together the security/residency appendix and need a concise, RFP-friendly clarification of Redwood's deployment footprint and routing/failover behavior. Specifically: 

- For EU-only requirements, can you state which Redwood deployment modes support zero-processing outside the EU (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and any caveats?
- If we use Redwood Private (VPC) deployed into eu-west-1, what components (control plane, logging, audit) still leave the region, if any?
- APAC fallback question: if we designate EU as primary but allow APAC for latency-sensitive end users, how do you describe data residency and egress in the RFP? Is there a short declarative statement we can include?
- Network diagrams (simple): list of hosting regions you operate in and supported failover order for production workloads.

We received an initial copy of the RFP (attached Section A). Can you get back to us with a short technical statement + a diagram we can include? Procurement would like a targeted reply by EOD Feb 12.

Attachments: [Attachment: NordicBank_RFP_SectionA.pdf (PDF, 320KB)]

Thanks,
Sven Larsson
Head of Cloud Procurement
NordicBank

Sven — thanks for the clear list. We can definitely provide an RFP-ready statement and a diagram. High-level answers below; Marcus and Jonas are looped for technical confirm.

Summary (short bullets you can drop into the RFP):
- Redwood supports three deployment modes: Hosted API (multi-tenant), Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (customer-managed VPC / on-prem).
- For strict EU-only processing, Redwood Private deployed to a customer-managed VPC in eu-west-1 ensures inference compute and model state remain in-customer subnets. In that configuration, no inference payloads are sent outside the selected region for processing.
- Control plane metadata (service control messages) can be hosted in a separate region per customer contract; for Private customers we offer an option for a customer-controlled control plane region or limited control-plane replication to an agreed region — we will provide a contractual commitment if required.
- Where Hosted or Dedicated is used, we publish the runtime region that processes requests; Hosted may route based on latency/policy and could process outside EU unless explicitly configured or contractually restricted.

Details (short form):
- Private (VPC) mode: All inference traffic terminates on instances in the customer's VPC. Data-at-rest can be protected with customer KMS (BYOK). Logs and audit records written to customer-managed storage in the same region when required.
- Dedicated: Provisioned GPU pools can be pinned to an EU region; telemetry/control-plane calls may still traverse a Redwood control plane endpoint unless Private control plane is selected.
- Hosted API: Designed for global low-latency; defaults to region routing and may process outside EU for global scaling; contractual data residency restrictions are available on an enterprise plan.

Attachments: I attached a regional footprint diagram and an initial RFP paragraph draft for your review.

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_Regional_Footprint_v1.pdf (PDF, 480KB)]

Proposed next step: Marcus will follow up with the narrow technical points you flagged (control-plane replication, logging, and BYOK behavior). If that looks good we can provide a one-paragraph declarative statement for the RFP and a PNG diagram.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Hi Sven,

Following Irene's summary, a few technical clarifications you can include verbatim in the RFP appendix: 

1) Private (VPC) mode — EU-only guarantee
- When Redwood Private is deployed into a customer VPC in eu-west-1, inference compute, model KV caches, and runtime ephemeral state remain in-customer subnets. We do not export inference payloads to other regions for processing.
- Customer-managed storage and KMS (BYOK) options ensure keys and at-rest objects remain in the same region.
- Control-plane traffic (deployment orchestration, health checks) by default goes to Redwood's control plane endpoints; however, for Private enterprise customers we offer a customer-controlled control plane deployment option (single-region control plane) and a contractual commitment that telemetry/audit copies will not leave the primary region.

2) Dedicated — pinned-region behavior
- Dedicated GPU pools can be pinned to eu-west-1. Runtime traffic will be served from the pinned region. System telemetry may still be sent to our control plane unless you select private control plane mode.

3) Hosted API — global default and policy-driven routing
- Hosted API is global by default and will choose runtime regions for latency/cost. In RFP language: "Hosted requests are routed to the nearest available runtime and may be processed outside the EU unless explicitly contracted otherwise."

4) APAC fallback and failover behavior
- Failover is policy-driven: customers may configure strict residency (no cross-region failover) or allow cross-region failover for availability. If APAC is permitted as a fallback, PII inference payloads may be routed to APAC run-times; we recommend documenting the allowed fallback regions and obtaining explicit customer consent.

5) Logging and audit records
- We can configure logs/audits to write to customer-controlled storage in the primary region. By default some operational logs are retained briefly in the control plane for support; this behavior can be removed under enterprise contracts.

Attachment: [Attachment: KMS_Integration_Guide.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

If you want, I can produce a one-paragraph "RFP declarative statement" that asserts EU-only processing when Private VPC in eu-west-1 + private control plane is selected. Draft below — if this meets requirements we'll provide it as a signed statement on Redwood letterhead:

"Declarative draft (for RFP): When Redwood Private is deployed to a customer-managed VPC in eu-west-1 and a customer-controlled control plane is selected, Redwood will ensure that inference requests, model state, and customer-managed logs are processed and stored within eu-west-1 and will not be exported to other regions for processing, except as required by the customer via explicit configuration. Customer-supplied KMS keys (BYOK) remain in eu-west-1 and are used for at-rest encryption of model artifacts and logs. Operational telemetry required for Redwood support is limited and can be contracted to remain in-region or be routed to customer-managed storage."

Let me know whether that paragraph is sufficient or whether legal needs a stronger contractual clause.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure Engineering
Redwood Inference

- The declarative draft looks fine; procurement wants a slightly stronger commitment line about "no processing outside the EU" that we can include as a requirement. Can you provide a one-sentence guaranteed statement we can paste into the RFP when the following conditions are met: Private (VPC) in eu-west-1 + customer-controlled control plane + BYOK?
- For the diagram, could you annotate the failover order and highlight which components are "in-region" vs "control-plane optional replication"? PNG is ideal.
- Please confirm whether audit logs (for 90-day retention) can be written exclusively to customer-managed storage in eu-west-1 with no copies stored elsewhere. If not, state the small subset of telemetry that would be retained outside region and why.

Procurement asks that we have the final text and the diagram no later than COB Feb 15 so we can include it in the RFP submission. If possible, please include a reference to the HubSpot deal (HS-3892) so we can match the RFP appendix.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 20-minute call — otherwise we expect the deliverables as attachments to this thread.

Thanks again,
Sven Larsson
